problem: Existing navigation world-model/VLA methods follow a loosely coupled 'envision-then-plan' pipeline, where future-frame imagination and action planning are separate, causing physical/causal inconsistency and accumulated prediction errors over long horizons.
motivation: Reliable real-world navigation needs both foresight (predicting plausible future observations) and planning (task-oriented actions). World models give dynamics but weak long-horizon reasoning, while VLAs give long-horizon reasoning but lack physical grounding, so tightly coupling them should give complementary benefits.
key_idea: Jointly model future video frames and action sequences in one generative framework, with a VLM planner conditioning both a Wan2.2 video diffusion generator and a policy head, coupled bidirectionally via cross-attention (MMFCA) and trained end-to-end.
insight: The gain is not from parameter scaling: a 7B VLM without the video generator gives 66.6 SR vs 66.5 for 3B on R2R-CE, while adding the video generator (3B) gives 67.9, suggesting the L_VG regularization/world-modeling supervision drives the improvement. Ablating the VG drops SR consistently on R2R, RxR and OVON. Sparse Foresight Scheduling shows the video branch is only needed intermittently (up to 6.7x speedup with nearly unchanged SR) because MMFCA is randomly disabled during training so the policy stays robust standalone.
method: VLM planner: Qwen2.5-VL-3B (pretrained on general VL data plus R2R/RxR/OVON, OmniNav-style) encodes instruction and historical/current multi-view observations into embeddings C (D=2048) that condition both video and action streams.

VLM-conditioned video generator: Wan2.2-TI2V-5B (LoRA rank 128) with the umT5 text encoder replaced by VLM embeddings via cross-attention; observations concatenated in batch dimension, history/current frames given near-zero noise, future front-view frames trained with flow matching (L_VG).
3D-RoPE rearrangement: current front/right/left views are placed side-by-side along the width axis (w, w+W, w+2W) with shared time/height indices to preserve spatial-temporal alignment.

Action policy heads: (i) Action Former, 5 learnable queries and 4 transformer blocks predicting (X,Y,cosθ,sinθ,arrival) with L1 + cosine + BCE losses; (ii) Diffusion Policy, 16 transformer layers trained by flow matching on action sequences.

MMFCA: bidirectional cross-attention (action-to-video and video-to-action) between the diffusion policy and the last 8 cross-attention DiT blocks of the video generator, with a binary switch γ; randomly enabled with 50% probability during training.
Two-stage training: Stage 1 trains video generator and policy head separately with frozen VLM; Stage 2 unfreezes all and jointly optimizes L_total = L_VG + λ L_PH.
Sparse Foresight Scheduling: Action Former variant runs without the video generator at inference; the Diffusion Policy variant activates video generation only every 10 steps to cut latency.

setting.backbone: Qwen2.5-VL-3B (full fine-tune) + Wan2.2-TI2V-5B (LoRA) + Action Former / Diffusion Policy head
setting.training_data: General VQA/grounding VL data for VLM pretraining; R2R, RxR (VLN-CE, Matterport3D) and OVON-style HM3D object-goal episodes with three-view panoramas, actions and waypoints; trained on 96 H20 GPUs
setting.observation: three-view RGB panorama (left, front, right) plus historical frames; no depth or odometry
setting.action_space: predicted waypoint sequence (X, Y, heading, arrival flag), 5 steps, executed as discrete forward/left/right/stop in Habitat
setting.simulator: Habitat (VLN-CE on Matterport3D, HM3D for OVON)

numbers_note: Ablation results for VG (Fig. 4a), SFS (Fig. 4b) and consistency (Fig. 4c) are only in figures. Table 3 gives R2R-CE SR: 3B w/o VG 66.5, 7B w/o VG 66.6, 3B w/ VG 67.9. Real-world results are only qualitative.
results: AstraNav-World beats the strongest baseline CorrectNav on R2R-CE (SR 67.9 vs 65.1, SPL 65.4 vs 62.3) and on RxR-CE (SR 72.9 vs 69.3). On HM3D-OVON it reaches 45.7 SR / 28.7 SPL vs 40.8 / 12.1 for MTU3D and 39.5 / 19.8 for Uni-NaVid. It also transfers zero-shot to a real robot without real-world fine-tuning, though shown only qualitatively.
limitations: Video generation adds latency and compute, needing Sparse Foresight Scheduling; performance in complex scenes is compute-limited.
Real-world evaluation is qualitative only (project page) with no quantitative numbers; the consistency analysis uses only 100 cases.
Most gains come from a strong VLM and extra pretraining; the video-generator contribution is modest (about +1.4 SR in the 3B ablation) and the VG ablation is given only in figures.
